agree.reason: The trend argument and checkpoint will reassure most members, but the two ad-background members are left asking why ads must end rather than run alongside membership while it grows, especially given the cash gap the memo admits for 2027.

honest.reason: The memo rightly turns the 'will replace within a year' claim into a goal and admits a 2027 shortfall, but it overreads the single peer newsroom ('shows the model can work'), and it treats the $84k year as the base for 2027 even though, in November 2026, that 'last year' is probably 2025.

works_the_facts.reason: The derived figures check out and are well framed: about 20% annual decline, $20,352 annual rate from the pilot, 1.5% conversion, 875 members = 6.25% of the list, 3–4x the pilot, and about $52k collected with steady growth; the 'costs us $17,000 more each year' line is muddled.

right_comparison.reason: The memo compares membership with ads on their declining path rather than a flat $84k, which is the right baseline, but the year projections may be shifted one year too generous to ads.

qualification.reason: The June 30 checkpoint of 550 members with options at the July meeting is concrete and checkable; the cancellation risk only promises reporting and sets no threshold, and the funding of the cash gap is left open.

objections.reason: It deals openly with cash flow and the long-serving colleague, but it never answers the obvious sales-side objection, 'why not keep ads and add membership', and its plan for the colleague is vague.

fit.reason: A tight one-page board memo with a clear decision request, headed sections and a recommendation.
